resolvedSinceRound1.finding: Resolved in site code, checked by reading the code; no browser run by RevScoresChopin. In src/assets/js/room.js the score loader now sets sc.end to the maximum note end (here 94.6 s). sheetView().draw computes past = t > score.end + 1: it then hides the highlight box and lights no noteheads. scoreCovers(t) returns the pitch readouts to live analysis past the same point. The built docs/assets/js/room.js contains the same logic (draw: `M=y>C.end+1`; `st(e){return!!C&&e<=C.end+1}`). For this side, the highlight goes out at 95.6 s, inside the noise-only gap (94.7–96.3 s) and before Op. 25 No. 9 starts at 96.4 s. Between 94.6 and 95.6 s bar 85 stays lit over its own decay.

observations.finding: The author's 74.54 s for bar 68 is right; the round-1 review estimate of 74.3–74.4 s was wrong. The D-flat6 rise at 74.33 s (+11 dB) belongs to bar 67's q133.5 (D-flat6 with the left hand's A-flat3/F4, published 74.293 s): F4 rises at 74.38 s (+19 dB) and A-flat3 at 74.25 s. q133.667 D-flat7 (published 74.381 s) rises at 74.39 s. Bar 68's downbeat (D-flat6 over G-flat3/B-flat3/G-flat4) matches the 74.58 s rises (G-flat4 +13 dB, G-flat5 partial +19 dB) and the D-flat6 rise at 74.61 s. Its second note, E-flat6, has no rise near 74.42 s (only +6 dB at 74.28 s) and a strong one at 74.66 s, so the sixteenth chain fixes the downbeat at about 74.54 s.
This is display only, unchanged: the 8a passages are engraved at sounding pitch with many ledger lines.
